criteria.title: 问题要具体到能决定分析怎么做
criteria.direct_rule: storyline-blueprint先恢复研究问题、困难、操作和结论。
criteria.inference: 从这一步反推：好论文不能只有“分析足球数据”这样的主题；应有能区分方法和结果的具体问题。
criteria.application: 本项目以“历史背景能在赛前实力之外增加多少预测信息”为主轴，保留三个RQ作为分解。

criteria.title: 贡献类型必须与证据相称
criteria.direct_rule: review rubric要求先识别理论、实证、系统或资源等贡献类型；writer禁止凭措辞创造更强贡献。
criteria.inference: 反推：不能用顶会算法创新的叙事包装一个未证明首创的整合研究，也不能因为没有首创就否认实证价值。
criteria.application: 定位为数据整理、动态实力与语境的整合以及共同样本实证比较；不新增“首次”“最优”或外部模型领先主张。

criteria.title: 方法必须解释操作为何回应困难
criteria.direct_rule: storyline要求定义对象/输入输出，解释操作及其信息依据，再在需要的位置给公式；研究工程技能要求机制与实际计算对应。
criteria.inference: 反推：列出Gaussian、Poisson、EP等名称不够。读者应能说明每部分处理什么问题、如何把信息交给下一步。
criteria.application: 连通不规则比赛、渐变/突变、场地解释、实力不确定性和联合预测；用公式已定义的梯度说明责任权重作用。

criteria.title: 核心主张必须能回到已有证据
criteria.direct_rule: integrity-auditor逐项追溯主张、数字、引用；reviewer要求先重建主张与支持再判断。
criteria.inference: 反推：文字不能比表格、推导或实验更强；同一主张在摘要、结果和结论中应有同一证据强度。
criteria.application: 保留原核心数值和推导；明确实力相关差异较大、语境增量较小，不能由相对损失直接分配信息份额。

criteria.title: 比较的完整方法、对象和口径必须一致
criteria.direct_rule: experiment-designer要求已报告比较核完整配置，并说明数据、指标与实验条件。
criteria.inference: 反推：比较是否可信，取决于是否在相同目标和可比条件下比较，而不是基线数量。
criteria.application: 保留21,413场同场比较、各自分母和完整跳变输入；分清“背景模型换成实力模型”与“在实力上增加语境”。

criteria.title: 不确定性应说清对象与覆盖范围
criteria.direct_rule: humanization要求保留相关假设、校准不确定性和技术术语；integrity要求区分不可比较与矛盾。
criteria.inference: 反推：实力后验、结果随机性和条件比较范围不能混称为“模型有置信度”；限定应解释一个具体推断问题。
criteria.application: 图中边际均值/标准差不等于完整预测输入；保留混合积分、条件生成器、固定系数范围与实际损失差无相依区间的边界。

criteria.title: 负结果和开发选择应解释结论怎么来的
criteria.direct_rule: writer和humanization要求保留负结果、协议事实及已观察/拟议区别；engineer区分运行失败与科学负结果。
criteria.inference: 反推：最终版本不是脱离迭代的成功故事。影响选择和适用范围的失败要保留，但不必逐句重复“不能保证”。
criteria.application: 保留低信息友谊赛偏差、数值近似失败、近年不及固定步长、初始化敏感和历史复用；把重复提醒改为选择风险的具体原因。

criteria.title: 各章要共同回答同一个问题
criteria.direct_rule: writer的整稿检查核摘要与结论是否描述实际工作；storyline按读者理解安排不同章节。
criteria.inference: 反推：一串研究题的流水账不等于完整论证。摘要提出的问题应在方法中落实，在结果中回答，在结论中解释意义。
criteria.application: 用“历史差异→日期相关实力→相同比赛预测→增量的地区/历史条件→前瞻使用”连接已有五部分结构。

criteria.title: 实验与检查要最小充分，而非清单越长越好
criteria.direct_rule: experiment-designer明确要求能够区分中心假设与合理替代解释的最小充分实验包，不为模板强加实验。
criteria.inference: 反推：好论文需要能回答问题的证据，不需要为了“显得严谨”不断增加无关消融或重复交叉验证。
criteria.application: 本轮复用既有数值/模拟/运行结果，不新增模型训练、消融或外部基线；未完成的未来成绩仍未完成。

criteria.title: 语言应直接表达研究，而不是内部验收或防御
criteria.direct_rule: humanization逐句恢复事实与作用，删除没有科学信息的辩护；prose guardrails规定检查器不是词语黑名单。
criteria.inference: 反推：正式语言不等于更多抽象名词、否定句或流程术语。限定要改变解释，词语是否保留取决于技术含义。
criteria.application: 改写配置身份、开发风险与结果意义的衔接，删除重复提醒；将leverage明确为对对数似然梯度的贡献。

criteria.title: 图表要展示科学对象并与文字同义
criteria.direct_rule: visual-composer要求保留值、单位、不确定性、标签与拓扑，并检查实际导出。
criteria.inference: 反推：图形不仅要好看，也要让人知道画了什么、能解释什么；不能把摘要图当完整分布或独立真实实力。
criteria.application: 7图5表保留原值，强化实力图的阅读方式并指回完整混合分布；未因通用建议重绘已有正确图。

criteria.title: 交付状态必须以实际产物区分通过/失败/未核查
criteria.direct_rule: submission-checker要求读真实构建与PDF，区分passed、failed、not applicable、unverified；common保留原始证据。
criteria.inference: 反推：论文写好了、编译过了、模型被现实验证了是不同状态。编辑报告必须说明实际做了哪些检查。
criteria.application: 更新当前源/PDF、差异和记录；保留原版与基线；不把本轮写作核查说成真人复核、完整复现或课程提交完成。

edits.before: Historical home-win rates in international football may reflect team strength, match composition, and venue-related conditions. This study assesses their contribution to pre-match prediction. Comparisons across eras, match types, and regions use 24,917 non-neutral matches from 1980--2024. A dynamic model estimates strength from earlier results, including eligible neutral matches; a joint model combines the resulting strength distribution with match context. Retrospective chronological evaluation compares background-only, strength-only, and joint predictions on 21,413 matches from 1990--2024. The joint model reduced log loss by 16.12\% relative to background alone and 0.42\% relative to strength alone, achieving 70.01\% binary accuracy for home win versus non-home win. Historical-window comparisons identified a trade-off between fitting cost and probability quality, without establishing a universally optimal window. Regional diagnostics revealed differences in robustness and probability bias, distinct from descriptive geographic differences in home-win rates. A prospective release contains 52 fixtures, with 49 main predictions and three withheld under the venue rule; outcomes remain unevaluated. In the aggregate loss comparison, strength provided the larger improvement. Context contributed a smaller increment, whose interpretation remains conditional on model assumptions and the reuse of historical data during development.
edits.after: Historical home-win rates combine differences in team strength, opponent composition, and match context. We assess whether context contributes predictive information after accounting for uncertain pre-match strength. The descriptive analysis uses 24,917 non-neutral matches from 1980--2024 to compare eras, match types, and regions. A dynamic model estimates strength from earlier results, including eligible neutral matches, and a joint model integrates that strength distribution with context. Retrospective chronological evaluation compares background-only, strength-only, and joint predictions on 21,413 matches from 1990--2024. The joint model reduced log loss by 16.12\% relative to background alone and 0.42\% relative to strength alone, achieving 70.01\% binary accuracy for home win versus non-home win. Historical-window comparisons identified a trade-off between fitting cost and probability quality without establishing a universally optimal window. Regional diagnostics showed uneven stability of the contextual increment and residual probability bias. A prospective release contains 52 fixtures, with 49 main predictions and three withheld under the venue rule; outcomes remain unevaluated. In this archive, strength provided the larger predictive improvement. Context added a smaller increment, whose interpretation remains conditional on model assumptions and historical reuse during development.
edits.reason: State the incremental-information question before methods and numbers; retain all numerical and retrospective/prospective qualifications.

edits.before: Historical home-win rates in international football are sensitive to the teams, opponents, competitions, and periods included in a sample. A high rate may reflect a strong home team or a relatively weak set of opponents. Comparisons across regions or decades must therefore distinguish differences in match composition from differences in performance. For pre-match prediction, the relevant question is whether these historical patterns provide information beyond the teams' previous results.
edits.after: A national team's home-win rate depends on its ability, the opponents it faces, and the matches included in the sample. Regional or historical differences can therefore arise from changes in match composition as well as performance. The forecasting question is whether era, match type, and geographic context remain informative once both teams' strength has been estimated from earlier results.
edits.reason: Replace a broad opening with the precise question answered by the comparisons.

edits.before: Descriptive comparisons identify differences in observed home-win rates; predictive analysis assesses their value for subsequent matches. An aggregate difference may provide little additional information once team strength is included, while agreement with the overall win frequency may conceal poor match-level predictions. National-team records present further challenges: irregular playing schedules, historical identity changes, neutral venues, and uneven coverage of opponent combinations. Analysis requires explicit sample definitions and a consistent account of the information available before each match.
edits.after: Descriptive rates and rating models address different parts of this question. Rates summarize observed outcomes but do not distinguish a strong home team from favourable opposition. Ratings summarize previous results, but their predictive value does not establish whether context adds information. National-team records further involve irregular playing schedules, historical identity changes, neutral venues, and uneven coverage of opponent combinations. The analysis therefore needs both date-specific strength estimates and comparisons that hold the prediction targets and information cutoffs constant.
edits.reason: Explain why both strength estimation and common-target evaluation are needed, rather than listing study components.

edits.before: We compare background-only, strength-only, and joint predictions on the same matches, examine historical-window length and regional applicability, and archive a prospective prediction release. In the aggregate probability-score comparison, strength accounts for the larger improvement and context provides a smaller increment. The results do not establish a universally optimal historical window or uniform performance across regions. The contribution is a documented analysis connecting historical comparisons to strength-informed prediction and its conditions of use.
edits.after:
The study combines a common cohort for historical comparisons, a model of evolving and uncertain pre-match strength, and chronological evaluation of contextual information. Background-only, strength-only, and joint predictors are compared on identical matches. This separates the predictive contribution of match context from the larger contribution associated with strength. Historical-window and regional analyses then examine when the resulting predictor is useful, and an archived release applies it to prospective fixtures.

In the aggregate loss comparison, strength provided the larger improvement and context a smaller increment. The tested history lengths favoured a cumulative default, while regional diagnostics qualified the stability of the contextual gain. These findings connect the historical patterns to a forecasting decision: whether context improves probabilities beyond what earlier team results already provide.
edits.reason: Link contributions to one research question and then state the findings and their practical interpretation.

edits.before: Dynamic paired comparisons~\cite{glickman1999dynamic} distinguish latent ability from uncertainty in its estimation. Gaussian evolution provides a tractable starting point: inactivity increases uncertainty without changing expected strength. A smooth diffusion alone may, however, adapt slowly to persistent abrupt changes. We therefore consider both the smooth special case and a model with persistent jumps. The latter was selected using the development criteria described below. This selection is conditional on those criteria; a simpler model can have lower error in a stationary simulation setting.
edits.after: Dynamic paired comparisons~\cite{glickman1999dynamic} distinguish latent ability from uncertainty in its estimation. Gaussian evolution accommodates irregular intervals by increasing uncertainty during inactivity without imposing a decline in expected strength. A smooth diffusion may adapt slowly to persistent abrupt changes, motivating the additional jump component. We compare the smooth special case with the jump model under the development criteria described below. The selected jump model satisfies those criteria, while a simpler model can have lower error in a stationary simulation setting.
edits.reason: Connect the process components to irregular schedules and abrupt changes while retaining the observed simpler-model advantage.

edits.before: TrueSkill~\cite{herbrich2006trueskill} incorporates uncertain skill, noisy performance, and a draw region, all relevant to an archive of home wins, draws, and away wins. Its application to game ratings does not establish its validity for national-team football. The time evolution, venue term, robust likelihood, and chronological checks used here require separate specification. Expectation propagation~\cite{minka2001ep} approximates inference across correlated latent states. Its use does not imply that the full posterior is Gaussian or that sequential inference is exact.
edits.after: TrueSkill~\cite{herbrich2006trueskill} represents uncertain skill through noisy performances and a draw region. These concepts suit an archive with home wins, draws, and away wins. National-team application additionally requires explicit time evolution and venue effects, which are specified in the present model. Expectation propagation~\cite{minka2001ep} approximates inference across correlated latent states; the resulting sequential posterior remains approximate.
edits.reason: Explain the transferable construction and the required adaptation directly, retaining the approximation limit.

edits.before: The remaining methods address distinct inferential tasks. Direct standardization compares observed rates under a common match composition. Proper scoring rules~\cite{gneiting2007scoring} evaluate probabilities assigned to subsequent outcomes. Simulation-based uncertainty analysis evaluates comparison procedures under specified generating mechanisms. These methods complement strength estimation, but model-conditional interval coverage alone cannot establish predictive superiority in real matches.
edits.after: The analysis assigns separate roles to match composition, strength, and context. Direct standardization compares historical rates under common compositions. The rating model interprets earlier results using both teams' latent strengths and a shared home term. The joint outcome model then receives the team-strength difference distribution, excluding that home term, and estimates its own context effects. This separation lets context be evaluated beyond strength while carrying strength uncertainty into the prediction. Proper scoring rules~\cite{gneiting2007scoring} evaluate those probabilities; simulation separately assesses conditional comparisons under specified generating mechanisms.
edits.reason: Replace a catalogue of tools with the dependency between the rating observation model, uncertain strength input, context model and evaluation.

edits.before: These parameters define the full-jump ratings used in the joint analysis. The archived rating report specifies these parameters. An earlier rule-evaluation exercise used a separate zero-jump special case. Table~\ref{tab:predictive-models} uses the full-jump input and the v2 annual prediction protocol; the supporting guide gives the exact configuration and output identifiers.
edits.after: The joint analysis uses the full-jump specification recorded in the archived rating report. The zero-jump special case used in an earlier rule-evaluation exercise is a separate reference, rather than the input to Table~\ref{tab:predictive-models}. That comparison uses the full-jump ratings and the v2 annual prediction protocol; exact configuration and output identifiers are listed in the supporting guide.
edits.reason: Preserve the important method-identity distinction while replacing workflow-status wording with the actual configuration relationship.

edits.before: The strength model was evaluated separately before its inclusion in the joint predictor. Its primary output is a time-indexed distribution of latent ability; true team strength is not observed. Figure~\ref{fig:strength-states} illustrates this output for four teams selected for presentation, rather than on the basis of predictive performance. Each point represents the state immediately before the selected match, excluding that match's result. The estimates incorporate both home and away appearances. Whiskers represent marginal uncertainty on the model's fixed performance-noise scale. They neither measure independently observed football quality nor account for all model error, and should not be interpreted as confidence intervals for true ability.
edits.after: The strength model produces a time-indexed distribution of latent ability for each team. Figure~\ref{fig:strength-states} illustrates the output for four teams selected for presentation rather than predictive performance. Each point is a pre-match estimate that excludes the selected match's result and incorporates earlier home and away appearances. The means summarize estimated strength, while the whiskers show marginal uncertainty on the fixed performance-noise scale. These marginal summaries distinguish estimated ability from its uncertainty. The joint model uses the strength-difference mixture in Equation~\ref{eq:difference-mixture}, rather than only the displayed mean and standard deviation.
edits.reason: Give the illustrative rating figure a scientific reading before the calibration and implementation diagnostics; detailed interval caveats remain in its caption.

edits.before: Including strength produced the larger reduction in loss (Table~\ref{tab:predictive-models}; Figure~\ref{fig:predictive-models}). Mean log loss declined from $0.671936$ for background alone to $0.566020$ for strength alone and $0.563630$ for the joint predictor. The joint model's relative reductions were $16.12\%$ against background alone and $0.42\%$ against strength alone. The absolute reductions were 0.105916 from background to strength and 0.002390 from strength to the joint model. These are aggregate loss comparisons, not an additive decomposition of information or evidence for individual subgroups. Binary accuracy followed the same ordering: $58.19\%$, $69.83\%$, and $70.01\%$. Accuracy refers to home-win/non-home-win classification and is distinct from relative loss reduction.
edits.after: The largest loss difference was between context-only and strength-only prediction (Table~\ref{tab:predictive-models}; Figure~\ref{fig:predictive-models}). Mean log loss was $0.671936$ for background alone, $0.566020$ for strength alone, and $0.563630$ for the joint predictor. The joint model's relative reductions were $16.12\%$ against background alone and $0.42\%$ against strength alone. The absolute reductions were 0.105916 from background to strength and 0.002390 from strength to the joint model. These comparisons identify the larger strength-related difference and the smaller contextual increment; they do not form an additive decomposition of information. Binary accuracy followed the same ordering: $58.19\%$, $69.83\%$, and $70.01\%$. Accuracy refers to home-win/non-home-win classification and is distinct from relative loss reduction.
edits.reason: Distinguish replacing context-only inputs with strength-only inputs from adding context to strength; retain every metric and denominator.

edits.before: For RQ2, adding strength to background produced a larger aggregate loss reduction than adding context to strength. The relative reductions have different denominators and cannot be interpreted as additive shares of information or as results for every subgroup with a high home-win rate. The model draws on dynamic paired comparisons~\citep{glickman1999dynamic}, with study-specific jump dynamics, information weights, and an outcome model. The empirical comparison uses internal predictors; FIFA rankings, Elo, and other external systems were not evaluated.
edits.after: For RQ2, the larger reduction in aggregate loss was associated with strength, while context provided a smaller increment. Dynamic paired comparisons~\citep{glickman1999dynamic} convert earlier results into estimates of ability and uncertainty; the common-sample comparison then tests whether context improves predictions beyond those estimates. The result gives context a conditional forecasting role. It does not turn geographic or tournament differences in observed home-win rates into an independent measure of venue advantage.
edits.reason: Interpret the central comparison in relation to the original home-rate question; external-benchmark and denominator qualifications remain in Method and Results.

edits.before: Model revision introduces selection risk. Numerical-reference failures led to a revised integration order, and residual probability bias led to separate shape and drift corrections. These changes brought the system within the documented operational requirements. However, repeated inspection of the same archive can favour revisions specific to that history. Retrospective improvement does not eliminate this risk. The prospective release records predictions made before their outcomes, but neither its accuracy nor the benefit of subsequent refinements is yet known.
edits.after: Development results changed both the integration procedure and probability correction: numerical-reference failures prompted a new integration order, and residual bias prompted separate shape and drift corrections. These revisions addressed observed defects under the documented criteria. Because the same archive also informed those decisions, the resulting historical scores can favour revisions specific to that archive. The prospective release preserves predictions made before their outcomes and permits a later test on new matches.
edits.reason: Describe what the observed failures changed and why historical selection remains relevant, without repeating generic warnings.

edits.before: Chronological prediction excludes the current result from its own inputs, while development and model selection still reuse the archive. The historical evaluation is therefore not an untouched final test. Simulation results apply to the specified generators; no dependence-adjusted interval from real match data establishes the persistence of the small contextual gain. Deletion checks assess evaluation composition without reconstructing the learning history. Wider application requires prospective evaluation and continued regional diagnostics.
edits.after: Chronological prediction excludes each match's own outcome from its inputs, but it does not make a reused development archive an untouched final test. Simulation results apply to their specified generators, and no dependence-adjusted interval from real match data establishes the persistence of the small contextual gain. Deletion checks assess evaluation composition while retaining the original learning history. Prospective evaluation and regional diagnostics therefore address different remaining questions about model use.
edits.reason: State the distinct limits of chronological evaluation, simulation and fixed-prediction deletion checks once, each attached to its consequence.

edits.before: Pre-match strength provided the larger reduction in aggregate predictive loss, with a smaller increment from context. Historical-window and regional analyses qualify its application. The archived prospective release permits future evaluation, supported by documented data, model development, performance, and limitations.
edits.after: Within this international-football archive, strength provided the larger reduction in predictive loss, and context supplied a smaller increment whose stability varied across regional checks. Historical-window comparisons favoured cumulative history among the tested choices and identified a computation--prediction trade-off. These results support evaluating historical home-win patterns as additional forecasting information after accounting for uncertain strength. The archived prospective release applies that approach with explicit information dates and preserves its probabilities for evaluation when outcomes become available.
edits.reason: End on what the study establishes and how the historical comparisons inform forecasting, rather than an inventory of documentation.

edits.before: An outcome very unlikely under a particular state has small responsibility there, reducing its leverage relative to the informative likelihood alone.
edits.after: An outcome very unlikely under a particular state has small responsibility there, reducing its contribution to the log-likelihood gradient relative to the informative component alone.
edits.reason: Name the exact quantity changed by the responsibility weight: the log-likelihood gradient in the displayed derivation, rather than unspecified leverage.
